family_title_en: Choose the words with a given long vowel

stages.ix_title: Choose the words with a given long vowel

prompt.en: Which word has this long vowel?

what_to_do.en: Tap the word with that long vowel.

stages.choice_rule: Four different whole words from the roots list or allowed_extra_words. The stem names one long vowel: long a, long e, long i, long o, or long u. Exactly one choice has that long vowel, and answer_index points to it. Move the right word to a new slot from item to item. Wrong words are kid words about school, home, food, pets, play, family, or weather. No misspellings, brands, real names, IPA, or lone sounds.

roots: The stem names one target only: long a, long e, long i, long o, or long u, using the letter name.
Offer four real whole words. Exactly one has that long vowel, and answer_index marks it.
Use correct spellings only. Do not put misspelled word-list forms in the choices.
Long a is the letter name in cake, rain, play, and baby. Cat, have, and said are not long a.
Long e is the letter name in tree, beach, and sleep. Head, bread, and bear are not long e. A final y, as in baby, puppy, happy, funny, and family, is long e.
Long i is the letter name in bike, kite, and night. Kit, give, and milk are not long i.
Long o is the letter name in boat, snow, and home. Fox, cow, clown, and flower are not long o.
Long u is the letter name in music, mule, and use. Duck, moon, blue, and food are not long u.
Tier 1 wrong words use an obvious different short vowel. Tier 2 may share a letter or be another long vowel. Tier 3 keeps a lookalike spelling with a different sound.
Stems and choices stay whole words or letter names. No IPA, no slash sounds, no held sounds, no brands, and no real names.

tier_rules.1: Short stem of about five words, such as Find the long a word. Three wrong words have an obvious different short vowel and do not look like the right word.
tier_rules.2: A grade-level question of about seven or eight words. Wrong words may share a letter or carry another long vowel. Two-syllable kid words are fine. Still only one word has the named long vowel.
tier_rules.3: A longer question up to ten words. Wrong words are near misses with a similar spelling but not the named long vowel, such as ea in head and bread or ow in cow and clown.
